behavior_items: The reproducer defines a small recursive type graph: `optional` inherits from `_Optional_base`, while `array<_Nm>` stores `_Nm` elements of type `optional` through `__array_traits<_Nm>::_Type = optional[_Nm]`. This means `array<8>` physically contains eight `optional` subobjects, and constructing an `array<8>` requires constructing those embedded `optional` elements.

`_Optional_base` has two constructors relevant to overload resolution: a variadic `constexpr _Optional_base(...) : _M_payload() {}` and a move constructor `constexpr _Optional_base(_Optional_base &&) {}`. The variadic constructor acts as a catch-all sink for arguments that are not `_Optional_base&&`.

`optional` has a templated converting constructor `template <typename _Up> constexpr optional(_Up __t) : _Base(forward(__t)) {}`. Its parameter is passed by value, so constructing `optional` from an `array<8>` first materializes a local parameter object `__t` of type `array<8>` inside the constructor invocation.

The custom `forward` is intentionally simplified and nonstandard: `template <typename _Tp> constexpr _Tp forward(_Tp &__t) { return static_cast<_Tp &&>(__t); }`. Unlike `std::forward`, it returns by value (`_Tp`) rather than by reference. As a result, `forward(__t)` does not merely cast; it creates a prvalue copy/move of `array<8>` from the named parameter `__t`.

Because `array<8>` contains an array of `optional`, evaluating `forward(__t)` requires constexpr construction of a new `array<8>` object from the existing `__t`. That copy/move of `array<8>` recursively processes its `_M_elems` array and therefore tries to construct each contained `optional` from the corresponding source element.

For each element, the compiler effectively needs to evaluate something like `optional(source_array._M_elems[i])`. Since the source element type is `optional`, overload resolution for the `optional` constructors is important. The class has an implicit copy/move constructor, but it also has the templated converting constructor, and the evaluation trace in the bug report shows GCC entering `optional(<anonymous>.array<8>::_M_elems[0])`, i.e. recursively considering construction from an element subobject during constexpr expansion.

Inside that recursive `optional(_Up)` instantiation, `_Up` becomes `optional`, so `_Base(forward(__t))` forwards an `optional` object to the `_Optional_base` constructors. The move constructor of `_Optional_base` is not viable for an `optional` argument directly, so the catch-all variadic constructor `_Optional_base(...)` is selected.

That variadic base-class constructor is unusual in a constexpr context because it receives a non-trivial class object through ellipsis. Clang diagnoses this as invalid/nonportable (`cannot pass object of non-trivial type 'array<8>' through variadic constructor`), while GCC 11 accepted the code and GCC 12 regressed by crashing instead of either accepting cleanly or rejecting with a diagnostic.

The declaration `} page { array<8> {} }` defines a global object `page` of type `optional` using list-initialization from an `array<8>` temporary. Because the constructors involved are marked `constexpr` and the object has static storage duration, GCC attempts constant evaluation of the full initialization sequence during compilation.

The constant-evaluation backtrace in the report shows the exact path: construct `page` via `optional::optional<array<8>>`, evaluate `forward(_Tp&)` with `_Tp = array<8>`, materialize `array<8>` from `static_cast<array<8>&&>(__t)`, then recurse into constructing an `optional` from the first array component `_M_elems[0]`. This demonstrates that the ICE is triggered while constexpr evaluation walks into a subobject of an array member during the copy/move of the forwarded `array<8>` value.

The crash site `cxx_eval_component_reference` indicates GCC's constexpr evaluator mishandles a component reference to a subobject reached through this recursive construction pattern. In other words, the compiler loses track of how to represent or access the referenced array element / member subobject during compile-time evaluation and aborts with an internal compiler error instead of producing a normal semantic result.

The reproducer is therefore not about runtime behavior; it is specifically exercising GCC's compile-time object construction machinery, including: recursive aggregate/member construction, forwarding implemented as value return, selection of a variadic base constructor, and constexpr traversal of array elements that are themselves class objects of the enclosing conversion target type.

The mention that adding the missing trailing semicolon makes the testcase valid is significant: the ICE depends on valid C++ syntax plus the specific initialization pattern, not on malformed input. The bug report also identifies the issue as a regression because GCC 11 accepts the testcase, whereas GCC 12 ICEs in the constexpr engine.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The testcase builds a self-referential construction chain: a global `optional page` is list-initialized from an `array<8>`, and `array<8>` contains eight `optional` members. `optional`'s templated constructor forwards its by-value parameter to the `_Optional_base` base class, but the custom `forward` returns by value, forcing constexpr construction of a fresh `array<8>` object. While copying/moving that `array<8>`, GCC recursively evaluates construction of its `optional` elements and then routes an `optional` argument into `_Optional_base(...)`, the variadic catch-all constructor. During this compile-time expansion, GCC 12 crashes in `cxx_eval_component_reference` while trying to reference an array/member subobject. So the reproducer exercises recursive constexpr object construction, array element subobject access, and variadic-constructor selection; the bug is that GCC 12 ICEs in the constexpr evaluator instead of handling the code normally.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The common pattern is a GCC 12 regression in C++20 constexpr evaluation triggered by recursive object construction with subobject traversal. The testcase forces constant evaluation of a global `optional` initialized from `array<8>`, where `array<8>` contains `optional[8]`, creating a self-referential construction graph. The templated `optional(_Up)` constructor takes its argument by value, and the custom `forward` returns by value rather than by reference, so GCC must constexpr-materialize a fresh `array<8>` object and recursively process its embedded `optional` elements. The failure occurs specifically when constexpr evaluation descends into an array element/member subobject (`_M_elems[0]`) and then tries to construct another `optional`, eventually selecting the variadic `_Optional_base(...)` constructor. The ICE location `cxx_eval_component_reference` strongly suggests the compiler loses or mishandles the representation of a component reference to an array/member subobject during constexpr evaluation, especially across temporary materialization / move-like propagation and recursive constructor expansion. Since GCC 11 accepted the testcase and GCC 12 ICEs, the likely defect is in changed constexpr evaluation logic in `cp/constexpr.cc`, not in parsing or general overload resolution.
possible_causes: Bug in `cp/constexpr.cc:cxx_eval_component_reference` when evaluating references to array elements that are class-type subobjects during recursive constexpr construction.
Incorrect handling of COMPONENT_REF/ARRAY_REF for subobjects of temporaries or materialized prvalues in the constexpr evaluator, causing invalid state when copying/moving `array<8>` by value.

Regression in constexpr object-construction logic for by-value forwarding patterns, where returning `_Tp` from `forward` forces creation of a new object and GCC mishandles the source-to-destination subobject mapping.

Failure in constexpr evaluation of recursive class construction involving arrays of the enclosing class type, leading to infinite/invalid descent or broken subobject bookkeeping rather than a clean semantic result.

Incorrect interaction between constexpr constructor evaluation and overload selection of the variadic base constructor `_Optional_base(...)`, especially when a nontrivial class argument is passed through ellipsis and subobject access must still be modeled.
Missing guard or fallback diagnostic in constant evaluation for unsupported/ill-formed ellipsis-based class argument passing, causing an ICE instead of graceful rejection or non-constant result.
Bug in constexpr copy/move evaluation for array members of class type, where the evaluator mishandles elementwise construction of `_M_elems[i]` and crashes on the first component reference.

State corruption or unhandled tree form in GCC 12 introduced by a regression in evaluating nested constructor calls that combine temporary materialization, base-class initialization, and component references.

The bug is a regression: GCC 11 accepts the valid testcase, while GCC 12 crashes, indicating a production compiler defect introduced in newer constexpr-evaluation code.

selected_files.reason: The ICE is explicitly reported in `cxx_eval_component_reference` at `cp/constexpr.cc:4136`, and the reproducer is entirely about recursive C++ constant evaluation of array/member subobjects during construction. This is the most direct and likely bug location.

The failure path involves recursive object construction, base-class initialization, array element construction, and materialization of by-value temporaries. `cp/init.cc` is responsible for high-level class initialization mechanics and is a plausible source of malformed trees or initialization structure later mishandled by constexpr evaluation.

Constructor overload resolution is central here: the templated `optional(_Up)` constructor, implicit copy/move behavior, and selection of the variadic `_Optional_base(...)` constructor all depend on C++ call resolution. A regression here could steer constexpr evaluation into an invalid path or produce a bad call expression.

The testcase stresses array/member construction and initializer processing for class types, including recursive aggregate-like copying of `array<8>` and subobject traversal. `cp/typeck2.cc` may participate in building the component/initializer trees that `cxx_eval_component_reference` later crashes on.

If the crash is due to malformed front-end expression trees for nested constructor calls, temporaries, or component references, `cp/semantics.cc` is a secondary suspect because it helps build and manage C++ expression forms before constexpr evaluation.

Generate insns to zero all st registers together. Return true when zeroing instructions are generated. Assume the number of st registers that are zeroed is num_of_st, we will emit the following sequence to zero them together: fldz; \ fldz; \ ... fldz; \ fstp %%st(0); \ fstp %%st(0); \ ... fstp %%st(0); i.e., num_of_st fldz followed by num_of_st fstp to clear the stack mark stack slots empty. How to compute the num_of_st: There is no direct mapping from stack registers to hard register numbers. If one stack register needs to be cleared, we don't know where in the stack the value remains. So, if any stack register needs to be cleared, the whole stack should be cleared. However, x87 stack registers that hold the return value should be excluded. x87 returns in the top (two for complex values) register, so num_of_st should be 7/6 when x87 returns, otherwise it will be 8.
